comparison: Both evaluate the optogenetic system development (C3, C20, C22-C26, C37) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes light-dependent control and physiological relevance. Peer reviewers accepted the technical innovation but requested additional quantification details (Essential revision 2a-c), which were addressed in revision. Strong agreement on system functionality.

Perfect claim overlap (C27-C30, C32, C38) with both evaluating as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights microscopy data showing DAG changes and ZAP70 colocalization. Peer reviewers accepted basic functionality and DAG signal proportionality to kinetics, requesting higher magnification images for correlation details. Agreement on core observations.

Perfect claim overlap (C39-C40, C43-C45) with both evaluating as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the systematic decoupling of occupancy from half-life and strong correlation evidence. Peer reviewers accepted this as the core experimental finding demonstrating kinetic proofreading. Strong agreement that this represents primary evidence.

Perfect claim overlap (C46-C47) but divergent evaluations. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with acknowledgment of caveats. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, initially rejecting the quantification ('estimate of 3 proofreading steps is undoubtedly wrong') and noting even after revision 'the proof of KP is not advanced that much in practice.' Major disagreement on validity of n=2.7 quantification.

Perfect claim overlap (C53-C55) but divergent evaluations. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, viewing ZAP70 data as clearly localizing proofreading to proximal pathway. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether lack of proofreading at ZAP70 reflects true biology or experimental artifact from the adhesion system. Significant disagreement on interpretation.

Perfect claim overlap (C48-C52) with both evaluating as SUPPORTED. OpenEval views the conclusion that kinetic proofreading is necessary but insufficient as logically sound. Peer reviewers accepted this as appropriately cautious after requesting better citation of alternative mechanisms. Agreement on limitations and need for additional mechanisms.

Perfect claim overlap (C33-C35) with both evaluating as SUPPORTED. OpenEval treats these as system validation measurements. Peer reviewers explicitly requested these quantifications (Essential revision 2a-b) and accepted them after revision ('these densities are now specified'). Agreement on characterization data validity.

Perfect claim overlap (C36) with both evaluating as SUPPORTED. OpenEval views this qualitative observation as motivating subsequent quantitative analysis. Peer reviewers accepted it as contributing to evidence that 'DAG reporter signal is proportional to kinetics rather than occupation.' Agreement on observational finding.

Perfect claim overlap (C56-C60) but divergent evaluations. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, viewing the anti-β2m control as validating that CD45 exclusion doesn't drive proofreading. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN with substantial concerns about the adhesion system throughout multiple rounds, with unresolved questions about residual adhesion in the off state. Major disagreement on control validity.

Perfect claim overlap (C2, C17-C19) with both evaluating as SUPPORTED. OpenEval views these as well-established field limitations motivating the optogenetic approach. Peer reviewers accepted this as valid motivation, acknowledging the difficulty of changing half-life while maintaining constant affinity. Agreement on rationale and background.

High claim overlap (C61-C65, C67; peer also includes C66) with both evaluating as SUPPORTED. OpenEval views the mechanistic interpretation about Lck's role as reasonable. Peer reviewers accepted with caveats, requesting careful statements about ZAP70 and appropriate literature citation. Agreement on mechanistic interpretation with appropriate caution.

Partial claim overlap (C1, C4 shared; OpenEval includes C9-C13, peer includes C69-C71). OpenEval rates central conclusion as SUPPORTED by comprehensive evidence. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating the paper 'does not resolve' the self/non-self discrimination question and has 'limited relevance to how a TCR works,' though acknowledging it 'could be published' as a technical tool. Major disagreement on broader significance.

Moderate claim overlap (C69-C71 shared; peer also includes C1, C4). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on comparison to companion study and proximal pathway localization. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN regarding broader TCR relevance but accept the comparison between CAR and TCR systems. Partial agreement on comparative findings but disagreement on implications.

Moderate claim overlap (C5-C8, C14-C16 shared; OpenEval includes additional background claims C41-C42, C66, C68). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval treats these as background knowledge with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers accepted after criticizing selective citation and requesting additional references (Essential revision 4). Agreement on background validity after revision.
